punchline: Capital shrank 36 percent while the positions stayed put: the cushion thinned after a good year.
thirty_sec: At the end of 1997 LTCM returned about 2.7 billion dollars to investors and cut its capital to 4.8 billion without shrinking its positions; balance-sheet leverage stood at 28 to 1.
question: In something going well, which cushion have you shrunk only because it is going well?
key_contrast: The positions did not grow; the cushion shrank and leverage rose.
